title: Fybroc Flange Configuration Difference: Nomenclature V5 vs V6
description: Documents the structural difference in how flange type is represented between Nomenclature V5 and V6 workbooks.

structural_change_summary.v5_approach: Combined single field: Series encodes both pump series AND flange type as one composite value (e.g. '1500 (ANSI)') mapped to a single hex letter.
structural_change_summary.v6_approach: Split into two independent fields: 'Series' (bare number, e.g. '1500') and 'Flange Type' (descriptor, e.g. 'ANSI'). The hex code is derived from the combination lookup in the Attributes sheet.
structural_change_summary.impact: V6 enables independent selection of series and flange type, allowing the same series to support multiple flange standards without duplicating series entries.

v5_series_field.description: Single field that combines series number + flange standard into one value, mapped to a single hex code.

v6_authoritative_flange_logic.source: Verified directly from Nomenclature_V6.xlsm formulas and defined names (not inferred).
v6_authoritative_flange_logic.default_evidence: Smart Number input cell F15 (horizontal) / F40 (vertical) is pre-populated with 'ANSI'.

series_code_derivation.explanation: Two-axis exact match on BOTH series AND flange type against the Attributes Series+Flange->Code table (rows 23-42), returning the single-letter code from column H.

v6_authoritative_flange_logic.constraint_enforcement: There is NO data validation restricting the flange cell. The valid series+flange combinations are enforced implicitly by the XLOOKUP table: only series 1500/1530/1600/1630 have DIN (codes I-L) and JIS (codes M-P) rows. All other series (2530, 3000, 5500, 5530, 6000, 7500, 7530, 8500) have ANSI rows only. Selecting an unsupported series+flange pair (e.g. 5500 + DIN) yields no XLOOKUP match (#N/A), which is how the workbook rejects it.
v6_authoritative_flange_logic.configurator_implementation_rule: Flange defaults to ANSI. Offer DIN/JIS only for series 1500/1530/1600/1630; for all other series, ANSI is the only valid flange. Derive the series segment code by exact (series, flange) match against the Attributes Series+Flange table - never by series alone.

rev03_v6_flange_source_resolution.authority_model: V6 and Rev0.3 are TIED TOGETHER, not competing. Rev0.3 BUILDS the configurator (field hierarchy, per-series option availability, selection flow/constraints the user navigates). V6 is the authoritative list of ALL allowable selections and their HEX MAPPING (which codes exist, which combinations are valid, part-number generation). A configuration is valid only when BOTH agree: Rev0.3 says it is selectable AND V6 has a hex code for it.
rev03_v6_flange_source_resolution.v6_hex_gate: The V6 Attributes Series+Flange->Code table (rows 23-42, codes A-T) is the complete universe of series+flange combinations that can produce a part number. DIN codes (I-L) and JIS codes (M-P) exist ONLY for series 1500, 1530, 1600, 1630. All other series are ANSI-only.
rev03_v6_flange_source_resolution.intersection_rule: Rev0.3 Selections marks DIN/ISO and JIS selectable for 2530 and 5500, but V6 has no hex code for those combinations - so they cannot generate a part number and are therefore not truly valid. Applying the both-must-agree rule, DIN/JIS are offered only for 1500/1530/1600/1630 (the intersection). No new part-number codes are invented; V6's hex mapping is the gate on buildable configurations.
rev03_v6_flange_source_resolution.configurator_rule: Flange defaults to ANSI (Rev0.3 STD marker + V6 F15 default). Offer DIN/JIS only where V6 has a hex code: series 1500/1530/1600/1630. For every other series, ANSI is the only flange offered.

series_field.description: Pure series number without flange information. Used as one axis of the series+flange code lookup.

flange_type_field.sheet: Attributes (Series+Flange lookup table) and Smart Number (segment derivation)
flange_type_field.description: Independent flange standard field. Selected separately from series. Combined with series to derive the hex code.

combined_lookup_table.description: Two-axis lookup: (Series, Flange Type) -> single hex code. Produces the same hex codes as V5 but via a structured join rather than a composite string.

flange_coverage_by_series.description: Which flange types are available for each series across V5 and V6. Coverage is identical - V6 did not add or remove any series+flange combinations.

v5.segment_position: Column E (position 2 in part number after Brand)
v5.derivation: Direct hex lookup from the composite Series field value.

v6.segment_position: Column E (position 2 in part number after Brand)
v6.derivation: Two-field lookup: user selects Series='1500' and Flange Type='ANSI' independently, then the Attributes table resolves the combination to code 'A'.
v6.example: Series='1500' + Flange Type='ANSI' -> lookup -> code 'A' -> part number position 2 = 'A'

smart_number_impact.hex_code_compatibility: FULLY_COMPATIBLE - same 20 codes, same meaning, same position in part number.

api_implementation_note.lookup_logic: API receives SERIES (bare number) and FLANGE_TYPE separately. The identifier generation function concatenates them as CONCAT(Series, ' (', Flange, ')') to perform the legacy-format lookup against cfg.fn_LookupIdentifierCode. This maintains backward compatibility with the SQL metadata which still stores the V5-format composite key.

key_differences.v6: User picks series (12 options) then flange type (up to 3 options depending on series)

key_differences.v5: Adding a new flange type requires a new composite entry per series
key_differences.v6: Adding a new flange type only requires adding it to the Flange Type list and adding lookup rows
Same constraint - only 1500, 1530, 1600, 1630 have DIN/JIS in the lookup table
Same — ANSI only for these series (no DIN/JIS rows in lookup table)

engineering_notes: V6's split design makes it possible to validate flange type independently of series (e.g., reject DIN for 5500 at the field constraint level rather than relying on the absence of a composite value).
The hex codes are 100% preserved between V5 and V6 — no migration of existing part numbers required.
The API bridges both worlds: it accepts the V6-style separate fields but reconstructs the V5-style composite key for SQL lookup compatibility.
